analyst.summary: HUL's Q4FY26 volume inflection (6% underlying volume growth, best in three years) is real and traceable to GST 2.0 price cuts and tax-relief-driven urban recovery converging with a decelerating-but-still-positive rural leg, but reported profit growth this year is substantially an ice-cream-demerger accounting artifact (PAT before exceptional items grew just 4% in Q4 versus a 20% headline), and the 3-year revenue CAGR of ~2% reflects a genuine structural deceleration in a highly-penetrated core portfolio facing real D2C share pressure in premium personal care. At roughly 33x trailing earnings versus HUL's own 55-65x historical premium, the stock has already de-rated meaningfully, and my reverse-DCF read finds a moderate, not extreme, growth-expectation gap. Hold: quality and the balance sheet are not in question, but this is priced for a recovery that a widely-anticipated Q1FY27 print (28 July 2026) will soon test - not a name to sell into that test, nor one to add ahead of it.
